```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(RdistNN)
```

## Overview

`diagnostics()` reports localization and estimator-specific information from
a fitted object. NP/TDNN, CATE and PLQR use retained weights and model state;
paired-ratio/CLATE diagnostics reconstruct weights from cached ranks and
can evaluate deletion-score concentration. No nuisance models are refitted.
Target-specific exact-distance groups use their averaged rank weights, including deletion-based
concentration. These weights can change ESS and support. Candidate summaries
take minimum ESS and maximum weight/concentration over targets; inspect target
diagnostics for the individual profiles. A warning identifies block averaging
as a rule for which persistent distance-tie inference is not established.
For NP/TDNN and CATE, `nobs()` reports training rows; `n_eff` below describes
local weight concentration.

Warnings summarize one issue family per call. Exact-distance ties retain their
inference qualification; near-uniform DNN weights and high effective sample
size for signed TDNN weights have different interpretations. A later independent
report or plot can warn again. Base R warning controls and calling handlers
apply, including `options(warn = 2)`.

Paired-ratio and CLATE calls retain every target, including targets whose ratio
or requested interval is unavailable. One warning points to `status` and
`components`; inspect those tables before interpreting the other targets.
Negative denominators alone are descriptive, and intentionally disabled
uncertainty does not produce an unavailable-interval warning. Ordinary mean
fits instead stop if their computed estimates are nonfinite and request
rescaling.

Dashboard panels can omit genuinely absent optional extras. Invalid plotting
options, inconsistent retained state and unexpected rendering failures stop.
Errors for absent optional extras have class `rdistnn_extra_unavailable`;
invalid current state has class `rdistnn_state_error` and requires refitting.
Warnings inherit `rdistnn_warning` with a specific family such as
`rdistnn_distance_ties_warning` or `rdistnn_partial_result_warning`. Code should
use those identities when handling a recognized condition, rather than parsing
English messages.

The shared fields include:

- `n_eff`, `max_weight`, and top-weight shares;
- realized rank radii and weighted distance summaries when `dx` is retained;
- tuning metadata when a tuning spec was used.

Estimator-specific fields are added by the corresponding method:

- NP: weighted outcome mean, standard deviation, and outcome quantiles;
  signed TDNN weights do not define a probability distribution, so weighted
  SD and quantiles are `NA` when weights are negative. Weight concentration
  summaries then describe signed weights rather than probability mass.
- CATE: treated/control mass and propensity summaries;
- CLATE/paired ratios: component uncertainty, first-stage statuses, physical
  radii and squared deletion-score concentration; CLATE adds instrument support;
- PLQR: residual-regressor Gram eigenvalues and condition number.

NP/TDNN, CATE and PLQR target diagnostics require `W`, retained by default.
Use `return` including `"W"` for those fits. Paired-ratio/CLATE diagnostics
also work without optional weight or distance extras; see [their guide](conditional-late-inference.html).

## Nonparametric Regression

```{r np}
demo_np <- np_demo_data(n = 120, p = 2, design = "sinusoidal", seed = 1)

fit_np <- np_dnn(
  data = demo_np$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  x0 = demo_np$x0,
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  s = 4L,
  se = FALSE,
  return = c("W", "dx", "ess")
)

d_np <- diagnostics(fit_np)
as.data.frame(d_np)[, c(
  "target_id",
  "n_eff",
  "weighted_mean_y",
  "weighted_sd_y",
  "weighted_y_q50"
)]
```

For NP fits, `weighted_mean_y` equals the local mean estimate when the weights
are normalized.

## CATE Overlap

```{r cate}
demo_cate <- cate_demo_data(n = 150, p = 2, design = "hetero", seed = 2)

fit_cate <- cate_dnn(
  data = demo_cate$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  t_col = "D",
  m0_col = "m0_oracle", m1_col = "m1_oracle",
  e_col = "e_oracle",
  x0 = demo_cate$x0,
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  s = 4L,
  se = FALSE,
  return = c("W", "dx", "psi", "nuisance")
)

d_cate <- diagnostics(fit_cate)
as.data.frame(d_cate)[, c(
  "target_id",
  "n_eff",
  "treated_mass",
  "control_mass",
  "treated_share",
  "weighted_mean_propensity",
  "treated_ess", "control_ess", "weighted_propensity_q10",
  "weighted_propensity_q90", "top5_score_share"
)]
```

Overlap diagnostics are available when the fit was constructed from treatment
and propensity inputs. If `cate_dnn()` was called with only a direct
`pseudo_outcome`, overlap fields remain present but are marked unavailable.

Printing summarizes available arm information, propensity quantiles and
top-five absolute score-contribution shares; the data frame retains each
profile's values. CLATE distinguishes instrument support, clipped propensity
mass and squared jackknife-contribution concentration. These quantities have
different definitions and should not be interpreted interchangeably.
Clipping prevents undefined arithmetic but does not establish overlap. The
reported order fraction is descriptive, rather than a calibrated validity threshold.

## Experimental PLQR conditioning

PLQR diagnostics and specialized plots remain experimental.

```{r plqr}
demo_plqr <- plqr_demo_data(n = 160, p = 2, p_d = 2, tau = 0.5, seed = 3)

fit_plqr <- plqr_dnn(
  data = demo_plqr$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  D_cols = c("D1", "D2"),
  g_col = "g_oracle",
  mD_cols = c("mD1", "mD2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  density_col = "density_oracle",
  theta_eval = demo_plqr$truth$theta_true,
  tau = 0.5,
  x0 = demo_plqr$x0,
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  s = 4L,
  se = TRUE,
  return = c("W", "dx", "score", "ess")
)

d_plqr <- diagnostics(fit_plqr)
as.data.frame(d_plqr)[, c(
  "target_id",
  "n_eff",
  "gram_min_eig",
  "gram_condition_number",
  "jacobian_min_singular_value",
  "jacobian_condition_number",
  "theta_vcov_available"
)]
```

The PLQR Gram diagnostic is based on the localized residual-regressor matrix
`D - m_D(X)`. It is an identification and conditioning diagnostic, not a local
bread estimate.

## Tuning Metadata

When a fit uses `tuning = ...`, the diagnostics table exposes compact tuning
metadata without duplicating the full candidate grid into every row.

```{r tuning}
fit_tuned <- np_dnn(
  data = demo_np$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  x0 = demo_np$x0,
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  tuning = tuning_dnn_paper(lambda = 1.25),
  se = FALSE,
  return = c("W", "tuning")
)

d_tuned <- diagnostics(fit_tuned)
as.data.frame(d_tuned)[, c(
  "target_id",
  "tuning_name",
  "tuning_default_s",
  "tuning_grid_n_candidates",
  "tuning_lambda_default"
)]

attr(d_tuned, "tuning_grid")
```

Use `attr(d_tuned, "tuning_grid")` when you need the full candidate table.

## Availability Rules

- Missing `W` prevents NP/TDNN, CATE and PLQR target diagnostics. Stored grid
  summaries and paired-ratio/CLATE diagnostics have their own retained state.
- Rank radii and weighted metric distances require retained `dx`; otherwise
  those fields are `NA` with `distance_diagnostics_available = FALSE`.
  CATE/CLATE physical radii can still use retained observations in original units.
- If CATE treatment/propensity state is unavailable, overlap fields are present
  but marked unavailable.
- If PLQR residual-regressor state is unavailable, Gram fields are present but
  marked unavailable.

The [paper](https://jakobjuergens.com/research/#orthogonal-inference-conditional-z)
states the conditions for inference. These diagnostics do not check all of them.
